2027-04-09.title: Friday after New Sunday
readings: God was pleased to reveal his Son to me; the persecutor now proclaims the faith
The least among you is the greatest
2027-04-09.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after New Sunday.
2027-04-09.verse: But when God, who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not confer with any human being.
theo: Christ is risen! The Resurrection did not stop with the Eleven in the upper room. Some years later the risen Lord met a man who was hunting his disciples, and today St Paul tells the Galatians what happened to him. He hides nothing: “You have heard, no doubt, of my earlier life in Judaism. I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it.” He was zealous, gifted, ahead of his companions. Then everything turned, and not by his own effort: “But when God, who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles...” Notice the words. God set him apart, God called him, God was pleased to reveal his Son. Paul saw the risen Christ on the road to Damascus (Acts 9; 1 Corinthians 15:8), and he counts himself among the witnesses of the Resurrection. Paul does not reject his people or their faith; he speaks with respect of “the traditions of my ancestors” and later says that God has not rejected his people (Romans 11:1). His zeal was turned, not destroyed: the same fire that once persecuted would now carry the Gospel to the ends of the earth.

What did the newly called Paul do? Not what we might expect. “I did not confer with any human being, nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were already apostles before me, but I went away at once into Arabia, and afterwards I returned to Damascus.” Only “after three years” did he go up “to visit Cephas and stayed with him fifteen days.” A conversion needs hidden years. The Lord himself spent thirty years in Nazareth before three years of preaching. St John Chrysostom remarks that Paul went to Peter not to be taught as a beginner but to honour him as the first of the apostles (in substance). And the end of the passage is beautiful: the churches of Judea “only heard it said, ‘The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy.’ And they glorified God because of me.” The best proof of the Resurrection is a changed life. When people who knew what we once were see what we have become, they do not praise us; they glorify God.

The Gospel brings us down from the great apostle to a small child. “An argument arose among them as to which one of them was the greatest.” Jesus does not argue back. He takes “a little child” and puts it by his side, and says, “Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me; for the least among all of you is the greatest.” Paul learned this. The man who had been ahead of everyone called himself “the least of the apostles” (1 Corinthians 15:9). On this Friday of the Easter season, look honestly at your own past, as Paul did, without hiding it and without despair: the grace that turned Paul can turn anyone. Pray for someone you have given up on. Welcome a child, a newcomer or a person who seems unimportant as you would welcome Christ. And if an argument starts about who is greatest, at home, at work or in the parish committee, be the one who steps back.
outline: Ask: is there anyone I have decided can never change?
God set Paul apart and revealed his Son.
Arabia, Damascus, and fifteen days with Cephas.
Point 3 · The least is the greatest
A child placed at the Lord's side.
“And they glorified God because of me.”
live: Pray for one you have given up on (Galatians 1:23)
Name someone you think will never change, and pray for him or her every day this week.
Give your full attention today to a child or to someone others overlook.
2027-04-09.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you met Saul on the road and turned the persecutor into your apostle. You know our past, and your grace is stronger than all of it. Reveal yourself to us more deeply, and to all who are far from you. Give us the humility to welcome the least in your name, and let our changed lives lead others to glorify the Father. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The same risen Lord who appeared to Paul comes to us in the Holy Qurbono, to set us apart for himself and to send us out.

quick: Paul persecuted the Church until God, through grace, revealed his Son to him.
After his call he spent hidden years in Arabia and Damascus before visiting Cephas.
Jesus put a little child by his side: the least among you is the greatest.
2027-04-09.action: Pray today for someone you think will never change.
2027-04-09.question: When people see my life, do they glorify God?

family.explain: The disciples were arguing about who was the most important among them. Jesus brought a little child and made the child stand next to him. He said that whoever welcomes a little child in his name welcomes him. In God's family the one who is small and humble is the greatest.
family.intention: We pray for children who are not welcomed or loved.
family.ask: Ask: “How can I make someone feel welcome tomorrow?”

illus: A young man in Kollam was known in his street for fighting and drinking. His mother went every Friday to the parish church and lit a candle for him. Neighbours told her she was wasting her money. One year, during Holy Week, he went to confession for the first time in eleven years, after a friend of his died in a road accident. He changed slowly, with many falls. Some years later he was leading the youth group's visits to the de-addiction centre. An old neighbour who had warned his mother stopped her outside the church and said, “I have seen it with my own eyes. Your God is great.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you called Paul by your grace. Call us again today, and open our hearts to your word. Amen.
share: God called me through his grace (Galatians 1:15). Where has God's grace turned my life?
I went away at once into Arabia (Galatians 1:17). Do I give God hidden time to shape me?
The least among all of you is the greatest (Luke 9:48). Where do I still want to be the greatest?
interc: For those who persecute the Church today, that they may meet the risen Christ.
For people struggling with addiction, and for their families who wait and pray.
For new converts and the newly baptized of this Easter.
For children who are neglected or unwanted.
For humility among leaders in our parishes and communities.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your Son to Paul and made a persecutor into an apostle. Turn the hearts of all who are far from you, make us humble like little children, and let our lives give you glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today St Paul tells his own story: I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it (Galatians 1:13). Then God, who had set him apart before he was born, was pleased to reveal his Son to him.
Paul did not rush to the front. He went to Arabia, returned to Damascus, and only after three years went to visit Cephas. Conversion needs hidden time with God.

And the churches of Judea heard: the one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy. And they glorified God because of me (Galatians 1:23–24). A changed life is a witness to the Resurrection.
In the Gospel Jesus puts a little child by his side: the least among all of you is the greatest (Luke 9:48). Let us pray for someone we have given up on, and welcome the least in his name. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Once there was a man named Saul who hurt the friends of Jesus. Then Jesus, alive and full of light, met him on the road. Saul became St Paul, one of the greatest friends Jesus ever had. Nobody is too bad for Jesus to love and change. Can you pray today for someone who is unkind to you?

intro: Theme: “The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy. And they glorified God because of me.”
On Friday after New Sunday: the grace that called Paul, the hidden years, and the child at the Lord's side.

sub: God was pleased to reveal his Son.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one way his grace has turned your life.

q: Therefore, I will now allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Give God fifteen quiet minutes each day this week, before your phone and before your work.

sub: Welcome the least in his name.
q: But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child that is with me.
Whoever becomes humble like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Step back from one argument this week about who is right or who is first.

concl: The risen Lord turned the persecutor into the apostle, and his grace can turn anyone.
A changed and humble life makes others glorify God.
2027-04-09.resolve: Pray for one you have given up on, give God hidden time each day, and welcome the least in the name of Jesus.
